result.summary: BUG-1 is FIXED in code. Static review only; runtime claims (statement-sequence equality, bytes) rest on TEST-DESIGNER's tests in hosted CI. The step-20 FAIL is lifted and the INV-5 verdict for 2c-ii is RESTORED as PASS (conditional on the merge conditions below). VERIFIED against step-20: (a) resolution per foreign_keys field: ScopedWrites.reference_fields reads definition_json foreign_keys (field, references_entity; matches the fixture shape) regardless of promotion state; ScopedLookup.all_in_scope?/4 dispatches on the REFERENCED type's ScopeDeclaration.for_type: {:column,f} -> count of rows with record_id = ANY($ids) AND column = ANY($set), compared with the distinct id count; :tenant_wide -> existence only (same statement without the column predicate); :undeclared -> false with no statement; scope :none -> false, no statement; :latest source or absent column -> -1 with no predicate statement (fails closed); [] and :all -> true, no statement. Null/absent skipped; non-string, non-UUID and empty string -> :malformed -> refused, no statement. (b) ONE bound statement per field whether the id is in scope, out of scope or nonexistent: count_visible issues a single Repo.one; every field is evaluated (no short-circuit across fields); the reference lookups therefore give an identical SQL sequence for out-of-scope vs nonexistent (the shared prefix statements, definition read and ScopeDeclaration reads, are the same for both). (c) THREE POSITIONS: router create and PUT run check_new_scope_value (pure check_new_value, then check_references_of_type) after validate_schema and before Idempotency.from_body and put_legacy_original (C-3 holds for references); Records create/update run scope_new_references before the transaction (explicit tests assert no begin); scope_check_new repeats it inside the :scope_check Multi step after the old value check and before upsert_record_latest and the dual write. DELETE: no reference check (scope_check_new returns :ok for :delete). (d) NO ROW LOCKS added: lookups are plain SELECT count; the existing FOR UPDATE on the record row and sequence lock order are untouched. (e) FK BACKSTOP: write_entity_table_row maps Postgrex.Error code :foreign_key_violation to {:error, :scope_refused} only when ctx.scope is not :all; for :all the raw {:error, error} is returned exactly as before (tenant-wide 500 unchanged, issue #2832). The Multi failure surfaces as {:error, :scope_refused}, rendered Response.not_found with the same telemetry kind (:write_value) as every other scoped write refusal. No constraint name or message is logged or returned. (f) PUT: no exemption for an unchanged stored reference (fail closed, documented in the ScopedWrites and Records moduledocs, pinned by a test). (g) IMPORT: check_batch_references collects the distinct well-formed ids per FK field across the whole batch and issues ONE ANY(ids) statement per field; any malformed value, unresolved id or undeclared target refuses the whole batch with the existing generic 404 (kind :import), evaluated after check_batch and before run_import_mode, position-independent; upsert_by external_ref still refused wholesale for a scoped caller before any write; ImportUpsert unchanged (one-line scope annotation only). (h) INV-7: the only identifier interpolation is literal(^column) from a format-validated module declaration; record ids and the scope set are bound arrays (type(^ids, {:array, Ecto.UUID}), type(^set, {:array, :string})); no new Repo.query with string building. (i) Telemetry: closed atoms %{policy, kind}; no id, node, set, tenant or constraint name. (j) Residual TOCTOU (referenced row's scope column changed after the check; FK KEY SHARE does not conflict with non-key updates) is ACCEPTED and documented in the ScopedWrites moduledoc, the Records moduledoc and design r2b 5.3 item 7; no lock on the referenced row. NOTHING ELSE CHANGED since step-17 that I have not reviewed: files modified after step-17 completed are only records.ex, scoped_lookup.ex, scoped_writes.ex, routers/entities.ex and the design doc in lib/ (route_scope.ex, scope_resolver.ex, the route snapshot, the exam/scheduler/seed/import_upsert annotation files and the compiler are older than step-17), plus tests. The F-2/F-4 refactor is sound: scope_value_in_set delegates to ScopedWrites.check_new_value for both the old (stored) and new document; maybe_scope_check keeps exactly two clauses (:all adds no step; scoped adds :scope_check).

findings.title: import statement count is not literally equal for a malformed reference
findings.detail: Step-20 e(6) asked for equal statement counts across import reasons. A malformed value refuses its field without a lookup (as ruled in step-20 a: no statement for malformed values), so a batch whose only bad entry is malformed issues one statement fewer than an out-of-scope or nonexistent one when that field has other ids. This is a value-shape difference chosen by the caller, carries no record-level information (out-of-scope and nonexistent remain identical), and is not an oracle.
findings.required_action: None. TEST-DESIGNER's equality assertion should compare out-of-scope vs nonexistent, and treat malformed separately; no code change.

findings.title: Ecto query logging of the failed FK insert
findings.detail: The scoped FK-violation backstop returns a closed atom, but Ecto's own query logger (pre-existing, all tenants) may log the failed insert. Not new, not a response leak.

result.ac23_verdict_sentence: SECURITY-REVIEWER code gate for REQ-518 2c-ii: PASS_WITH_FINDINGS after the BUG-1 fix (reference fields of a scoped write are resolved through the scope of the referenced type in the router, in Records and inside the transaction, with a foreign-key-violation backstop, so an out-of-scope and a nonexistent reference are indistinguishable; handoffs step-17, step-20 and step-21); exactly fifteen routes are reclassified from the default tenant_wide class (seven entity definition/restriction routes to an explicit tenant_wide declaration; the eight entity record write, import and record attachment routes to a resolver class), exactly those fifteen lines are removed from test/fixtures/route_scope/tenant_wide_default_routes.txt (137 to 122), and a scoped caller's import with upsert_by external_ref is refused with the generic 404 because the upsert primitive is not scope-aware.
